w10_T4_000189: A film club had 163 leaflets stacked in its office and a member brought in 32 more. 140 of the leaflets were handed out to commuters at the railway station. Each leaflet still in the office was folded around 7 discount vouchers for the club's next season. The club then reprinted the vouchers so that the office held twice as many as it had before. Half of all those vouchers were driven over to the club's second venue across the city, and a spilled cup of coffee ruined 169 of the ones that stayed behind. How many vouchers are still usable in the office?
w10_T4_000194: Early on Saturday morning a bakery pulled 217 trays out of the oven, with 5 buns on every tray. Through the rest of the morning 661 buns were sold across the counter. In the afternoon a second bake added 73 buns to the shelves. In the evening a food bank van collected 60 buns for its weekend parcels. A dozen pigeons waited outside the door for crumbs. The till roll prints every price in cents rather than dollars. How many buns are left on the shelves?
w10_T4_000196: On Monday morning a joinery workshop cut 194 planks, and every plank yielded 6 slats. Later that morning 1083 slats were used up building flat-pack shelving kits. In the afternoon a supplier delivered 70 more slats, and the foreman rejected 42 that had warped in the damp. In the evening the owner ordered a second batch identical to what was in the store, so the store ended up holding 2 times its late-afternoon count. The workshop's band saw is 3 years old. How many slats are in the store now?
w10_T4_000197: A summer camp owns 138 tents, but 15 of them were torn in a storm and taken out of service. Every tent that is still usable sleeps 2 campers. A further 74 campers are staying in the wooden cabins by the lake. Each camper at the site is issued 6 meal tickets for the week, and every meal ticket can be exchanged for 8 tokens at the canteen. The lake is 3 kilometres across at its widest point. How many tokens could the campers claim altogether?
w10_T4_000200: On Monday morning a nursery school took delivery of 207 boxes of crayons, and each box held 9 crayons. Before lunch a parent donated 70 loose crayons to the same basket. During the afternoon the children carried 1664 crayons off to the classrooms. In the evening the staff threw away 21 crayons that had been worn down to stubs. How many crayons are left in the basket?
w10_T4_000203: At the start of the morning shift a hospital pharmacy had 71 boxes of bandages on the shelf. 17 boxes went up to the emergency ward before lunch. In the early afternoon a supplier delivered 51 boxes, and later the same afternoon a charity donated 76 more. In the evening the night team unpacked 31 boxes from a returned order and added them to the same shelf. A dozen staff are on the day rota. The corridor outside the pharmacy is 40 metres long. How many boxes of bandages are on the shelf now?
w10_T4_000205: A school held a sponsored walk in which 138 pupils each completed 6 laps of the field. The teachers walked 55 laps between them and added those to the school's total. Each lap of the field is made up of 2 circuits of the inner running track. A local business promised 9 cents for every circuit walked. The sponsorship form records the promise in cents rather than in dollars. How many cents does the business owe the school?
w10_T4_000206: A fruit stall opened the day with 14 crates of strawberries, and a café bought 4 crates whole before the market filled up. The stallholder unpacked the crates she still had, finding 5 punnets in each one, and set them all on the table. She sold 43 punnets during the morning rush. A fresh delivery then left the table holding twice as many punnets as it had held just after the rush. A neighbouring grower added 65 punnets of his own to the same table. The stall's price board is written in cents rather than dollars. How many punnets are on the table?
w10_T4_000209: Nora had 17 boxes of wool in the loft with 9 balls in each box. She used 81 balls making a blanket for the winter fair. Her friend Hugo, who knits far less than Nora does, unwound every ball she had left into 3 shorter lengths for a beginners' workshop. The class got through 63 of those lengths on the first evening. The village hall costs 30 dollars an hour to hire. How many lengths of wool are left?
w10_T4_000210: A furniture repair shop had 41 wooden stools waiting for attention. 8 of them were beyond saving and were broken up for firewood, and a customer collected 24 that had already been mended. A house clearance then brought in 77 more stools that needed work. The joiner unscrewed all 6 legs from every stool in the shop and stacked the loose legs into bundles of 6. The shop's van holds 20 stools at a time. How many bundles of legs did the joiner stack?
w10_T4_000213: Priya's bookshop had 221 second-hand novels on the trolley one week, and a customer donated 27 more. She sold 93 of them at the weekend market and sent 109 to a charity shop, then pulled 16 off the trolley because pages were missing. Her business partner Sam matched what was left exactly with novels from his own store, so the shop's total became 2 times the trolley's count, even though Sam keeps less stock overall than Priya does. Every novel in the shop was then given 3 promotional bookmarks. The shop's ledger counts single novels rather than boxed sets. How many bookmarks were used?
w10_T4_000217: Tariq had 52 tulip bulbs in his shed and found 5 more in an old sack behind the mower. He gave 39 of them to the community garden and later bought 51 fresh bulbs at the market. His neighbour Wren, who plants far fewer bulbs than Tariq does each spring, told him that every bulb he had would send up 5 flowers. Each of those flowers opens with 9 petals. The garden gate is 3 metres wide. How many petals would Tariq's bulbs produce?
w10_T4_000222: A juice bar took delivery of 128 crates of oranges, with 3 nets packed in every crate and 7 oranges in every net. A neighbouring grocer sent round 65 loose oranges to add to the same store. The bar juiced 988 oranges during the festival weekend. The stock book counts single oranges rather than whole nets. How many oranges are still in the store?
w10_T4_000224: Maya brought 32 sheets of card to the art room and her classmate Ben gave her 47, which was more than she had started with. Every sheet was trimmed into 8 small cards for the display project. The class used 482 of the cards on the corridor wall, 82 were ruined by spilled glue, and 41 were posted home to parents. The clock in the art room runs 25 minutes fast. How many cards are left?
w10_T4_000225: A youth club was given 130 tickets for a football match and kept half of them for its own members, passing the rest to a partner club. 57 of the club's tickets were claimed on the first evening. A sponsor then sent the club 55 more tickets, and the stadium's community office added a further 63. The club's noticeboard lists tickets one by one rather than in whole blocks. How many tickets does the youth club have left to give out?
w10_T4_000229: The hostel laundry counted 158 clean towels on the shelf on Wednesday. Housekeeping returned 11 towels that had never been used, and a supplier delivered 57 fresh ones. The manager threw out 23 towels that had gone threadbare and sent 51 across to the hostel's other branch. A dozen guests were waiting in the lobby while she counted. The laundry's stock sheet is written in single towels rather than in bales. How many towels are on the shelf now?
w10_T4_000232: On Monday morning a dairy round set off with 130 bottles of milk on the float. A depot worker had added 12 bottles just before the driver, Femi, pulled away. Femi delivered 45 bottles on the first street. At midday his colleague Rosa, who runs a shorter round than Femi does, handed him 11 bottles left over from her own float, and in the afternoon the depot topped him up with 38 more. In the evening the dairy credited 8 loyalty points for every bottle still on Femi's float. How many loyalty points were credited?
w10_T4_000233: Nadia and Ivo run a ribbon workshop together. Nadia measured out 188 metres of ribbon and divided it equally between the 2 benches, and Ivo, who works the slower bench, took one of those shares. Every metre on Ivo's bench was cut into 8 short lengths. Each short length was folded into 3 loops for a rosette. The binding machine takes 2 loops at a time and makes one bind for each pair, and every bind is fastened with 3 stitches. Each stitch uses 7 centimetres of thread. How many centimetres of thread did Ivo's bench use?
w10_T4_000240: A model railway club stored its track in 20 boxes, with 5 pieces of track in every box. 20 pieces were found warped and thrown out, and 52 were sold on to another club. The club then bought 6 metal joining pins for every piece of track still in the store, and a spare tin in the cupboard already held 16 loose pins. A dozen members turned up to the Tuesday meeting. How many pins does the club have now?
w10_T4_000242: On Friday morning the cinema staff opened up 89 rows of seats, with 9 seats in every row. During the afternoon screening 380 of the seats were taken. At the early evening show a further 349 seats were sold. Later that evening 26 seats were roped off because the roof above them had started to leak. How many seats are still free?
w10_T4_000249: A riding stables stored 204 bales of hay in the barn, and a farmer delivered 5 more before the frost came. The horses got through 124 bales over the winter. Every bale still in the barn was split into 8 hay nets for the paddock feeders. One very cold week used up 266 of those nets. A dozen ponies share the top field. How many hay nets are left in the barn?
w10_T4_000250: Ivan's phone repair shop had 221 screen protectors in the drawer, and a sales rep left another 48 on his counter. The shop sold 71 of them over the weekend. His business partner Dolores, whose branch keeps less stock than Ivan's does, took 90 for her own counter across town. Every protector left in Ivan's drawer was then packed with 3 cleaning wipes ready for sale. The shop's stock system counts single protectors rather than sealed boxes. How many cleaning wipes were packed?
w10_T4_000253: The stadium is divided into 109 blocks, every block has 7 rows, and every row holds 8 seats. At Saturday's match each seat holder was handed 5 raffle tickets on the way in. Half of all the tickets handed out were entered into the first draw of the evening. Each ticket in that first draw earned its holder 5 loyalty points. How many loyalty points were earned in the first draw?
w10_T4_000257: On Wednesday morning a florist had 99 roses standing in the cold bucket. Before noon 37 of them went into a wedding bouquet. In the early afternoon a grower delivered 17 more roses to the shop. Later that afternoon she tied every rose in the bucket into a posy with 3 sprigs of fern beside it. In the evening she noticed that each sprig of fern carries 9 small leaflets. How many leaflets are on the fern in her posies?
w10_T4_000265: On Monday morning a small call centre logged 177 calls, and each of those calls lasted 5 minutes. In the afternoon one very long call added 22 further minutes to the day's total. The phone company charges 4 cents for every minute of connection, and in the evening it added a further 45 cents to the day's bill for line rental. The office has 12 desks along the window. The bill is issued in cents rather than in dollars. How many cents does the call centre owe for Monday?
